jobs.jobDescription:
About Fieldguide

Fieldguide is the AI platform for audit and advisory firms. We are helping firms make the most consequential decision of the decade: not which AI tool to buy, but which partner to build their agentic firm with. Practitioner led, agent executed. We are Series C, scaling fast, and the firms we work with are rebuilding how professional services gets done.

The role

We are looking for a demand generation manager who thinks in funnels, not channels.

You will own Fieldguide’s campaign demand engine: the webinars, nurture tracks, email programs, and content distribution that build pipeline across every segment of the market. You will own the number for those channels, from the hypothesis to the honest read on what worked.

This is a hands-on program owner seat with real ownership. You will set the calendar, write the briefs, run the pods, and carry the outcome. You will work alongside a peer who owns paid performance, so you can go deep on the campaign side rather than spreading thin across everything.

You are also someone who uses AI daily. Not as a novelty, but because you have built workflows that let you produce like a team of three.

What you’ll do

Own the webinar program. Thought leadership, product release, and sponsored webinars. Content, production, promotion, registration and attendance conversion, and follow-up. Build it as a repeatable operating rhythm, not a series of one-offs.

Own nurture and lifecycle. Design and ship segmented nurture tracks by practice area, persona, and funnel stage. Instrument conversion before launch. Read it honestly. Kill what isn’t working.

Own email campaigns. Content launches, product announcements, pre and post event promotion. Every send has a hypothesis and a metric.

Own content syndication, distribution and segmentation. Take the content our brand and product marketing teams produce and get it in front of the right audience, in the right sequence, more than once. Define the audiences and the list strategy.

Orchestrate with ABM. Partner closely with our ABM lead so account-based plays have campaign air cover, a shared calendar, and the collateral they need.

Partner on the demand side of events. Catalyst, trade shows, and field events. You drive the demand campaign wrapped around the event: promotion, registration, and follow-up sequencing, alongside our Field Marketing team who own the event itself.

Report on what’s working. Own the campaign read in the weekly pipeline review: pipeline created and influenced by program, against pace. Build the reporting and the AI-assisted monitoring that surfaces a problem before anyone has to ask.

Use AI to multiply output. Ask whether AI can do the first 80% of every task, then spend your time on the judgment and the finish. Build agentic monitoring for campaign performance. Share the workflows so the leverage compounds across the team.

What you bring

  • 6+ years in B2B demand generation, campaign marketing, or lifecycle marketing, with clear ownership of a pipeline number.

  • Experience at the scale we are operating at: programs contributing meaningfully to a quarterly pipeline target in the eight figures, not a few hundred thousand.

  • Full-funnel thinking. You can walk through a program you owned and name the stages, the conversion rate at each one, the persona map, and where the leak was. Tactics are steps in a journey, never the whole story.

  • Deep hands-on experience with webinars, nurture, and email at real scale. You have this down to a science, not in theory.

  • Fluency in HubSpot or a comparable marketing automation platform. You build the workflow yourself; you don’t wait for ops.

  • A specific, demonstrable AI practice in campaign execution. You can show us the workflow, the inputs, and what it replaced.

  • Comfort in the seams. Much of this job is making the next function’s work easier: ABM, content, ops, sales. You bring dependencies in early and hand off cleanly.

  • A high bar you hold yourself. You are the first quality check on your own work, and you measure it against the best in the category, not against your last campaign.

  • B2B experience. Professional services, accounting, audit, or fintech is a plus; B2C is not a fit.

What great looks like here

We measure ourselves by outcomes, not effort. Great work doesn’t meet the standard, it sets it. Ordinary is the failure mode, even when ordinary is clean and correct.

If that sounds like the way you already work, we should talk.

Since 2019, Mercury has been rebuilding banking* for the way modern companies work. We combine thoughtful design with strong engineering to offer checking and savings accounts, cards, payments, credit, treasury and the analytics that tie it all together. Everything we build comes from one belief: finance should be carefully crafted, fast and transparent, and it should stay out of the way so founders can get back to building.

That belief only holds up if the right people are building it. Hiring is one of the most important ways we shape Mercury’s future. In this role, you’ll directly influence the teams building our products and the experience of our customers. As a Technical Recruiter, you’ll own a focused set of searches from kickoff to close and partner closely with hiring managers along the way.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What you’ll do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for engineering and data roles, from kick-off to close
  • Build and maintain strong, healthy pipelines across multiple roles simultaneously
  • Source candidates proactively and creatively to engage top technical talent
  • Develop a deep understanding of Mercury’s products, engineering challenges, and team needs
  • Communicate clearly and consistently with stakeholders on pipeline health, progress, blockers, and recruiting timeline
  • Own offer strategy and closing for your searches
  • Deliver a candidate experience that's thoughtful and transparent from first touch to final decision

You should have:

  • 1-3 years of experience as a technical recruiter supporting engineering or data teams
  • Strong sourcing skills that go beyond LinkedIn Recruiter
  • Deep curiosity about the products and teams you support, and a strong understanding of how the roles you hire for drive impact
  • Strong alignment with Mercury’s values and ability to represent them authentically to candidates and your teammates
  • Enjoy building diverse, inclusive, and high-performing teams, and lead with deep empathy, kindness, and care for the work you do
  • Have a strong sense of urgency and ownership for the work you do, and be willing to help support hiring efforts across other areas of the business, as needed

Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. About Us

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by augmenting the work of assurance and audit practitioners with AI agents. The value we bring firms: Expertise, amplified. About the Role & Team

The Payroll Operations Specialist supports the compliance infrastructure that keeps our customers’ payroll operations running smoothly. You’ll own operational workflows across state registrations, employer account maintenance, workers’ compensation, business registrations, and related requirements.

You’ll work closely with Payroll Operations, Customer Support, Benefit, government agencies, insurance carriers, and external partners to resolve issues and deliver a strong customer experience.

  • Own end-to-end workflows across assigned areas, including state registrations, employer account maintenance, workers’ compensation, Foreign Qualification (FQAL), Registered Agent Administration (RAA), Statements of Information (SOI), and related requirements.

jobs.jobDescription:
About Us

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by automating and streamlining the work of assurance and audit practitioners — specifically in cybersecurity, privacy, and financial audits. We build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We're based in San Francisco, CA, and we're backed by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, and more. Over 50 of the top 100 accounting and consulting firms trust Fieldguide to power mission-critical work.

Role Summary

This role owns quality and automation for large enterprise deployments. You'll work closely with customers and our internal engineering team to develop a world-class QA Function that’s built from an agent-first lens.

We're building our quality and automation capacity around agentic tooling, and this role sits at the center of that: using agents to take on the repetitive work of finding, reproducing, and resolving issues, strengthening our internal testing, and keeping our SaaS and PaaS environments consistent. You'll also work directly with the customer on how issues get reported and resolved, and own the reporting that shows where quality is heading.

We're hiring across all levels. Depending on your experience and what you're looking to own, you may join executing against this scope, owning the customer's quality experience end to end, or setting quality and automation standards across Engineering. We'll calibrate seniority during interviews based on scope and demonstrated experience.

What You'll Own

  • Keep environments consistent across our SaaS and PaaS deployments, so behavior a customer sees in one place matches everywhere else and configuration drift doesn't become a defect

  • Build our automation capacity for handling bugs using agentic tooling including triage, reproduction, and routing that runs without a human in the middle

  • Use agentic tools to resolve bugs yourself, shipping fixes rather than filing tickets and waiting

  • Run bug bashes on new features before they're released, and make the practice repeatable enough that other teams adopt it

  • Own bug reporting and communication: severity-weighted trends, hotspots, and a clear read on where quality is heading that engineering leadership and the customer both trust

  • Work closely with the customer to integrate deeply with their processes and improve how they report issues, validate fixes, and decide something is ready for customers

  • Improve our internal automated testing: coverage where it pays, CI signal people believe, and less flake

  • Close the loop from a customer-reported issue back to the test or environment check that would have caught it

  • Support our evaluation efforts by creating and curating relevant datasets that can support agent quality

Who You Are (All Levels)

  • An engineer who fixes what you find. You're strong in the codebase and you'd rather ship the fix than hand it off

  • AI-native in how you work: you treat agentic tooling as core leverage for the unglamorous parts of quality, and you've used it on real work rather than just tried it

  • You think in trends, hotspots, and severity, not anecdotes, and you can tell a clear story from a messy bug backlog

  • Strong with customers: you can sit with a frustrated enterprise user, understand their process, and be the person they trust to get it resolved

  • Comfortable across the stack and across environments spanning application code, CI, and the deployment differences that make "works on SaaS" not mean "works everywhere"

  • Genuinely collaborative across the organization: you'll work daily with engineers, PM, support, and customer-facing teams, and treat that as the best part of the job

  • High ownership and comfortable with ambiguity. Nobody hands you the list of what to test or what to automate first

  • Able to internalize a hard domain fast. You don't need to know audit, but you'll learn enough to know what "broken" means to an auditor

Higher-Level Responsibilities

At the Senior level, you may:

  • Own the customer's quality experience end to end, including the reporting and communication relationship

  • Set the agentic automation strategy for bug handling and decide where automation pays and where it doesn't

  • Define what environment parity means across SaaS and PaaS and drive the work to hold it

  • Collaborate with PMs and engineering leads to shape release practice and quality gates

  • Mentor other engineers and raise the bar on testing rigor across teams

At the Staff level, you may:

  • Set and champion quality and automation standards across Engineering, beyond this one deployment

  • Drive company-level initiatives on release confidence, environment consistency, and defect prevention

  • Partner with engineering and product leadership to define long-term quality strategy

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to leaders across Engineering, Product, and Support

  • Represent Fieldguide externally through writing, speaking, and open-source contributions

Experience

Must-have:

  • Strong production software engineering experience — you write and ship code, not only tests

  • Hands-on experience building test automation and CI quality gates that engineers actually rely on

  • Real use of AI or agentic tooling as part of how you work

  • Experience working directly with customers or enterprise users on issues they care about

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and owning outcomes without a defined queue

Nice-to-have:

  • Python, TypeScript, React, Postgres, Hasura, GraphQL

  • E2E and integration frameworks such as Playwright or Cypress

  • Experience with both multi-tenant SaaS and single-tenant or self-managed enterprise deployments

  • Infrastructure exposure for environment parity work — AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform

  • Observability and tracing tooling such as Datadog

  • Experience building agentic workflows or internal tooling with LLMs

  • Performance and load testing, especially on long-running workflows

  • Security and compliance environments (SOC 2, FedRAMP, or similar)

  • Background in audit, accounting, financial services, or another regulated domain

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation with equity

  • Comprehensive health and wellness benefits

  • Flexible time off and work schedules

  • Technology reimbursements

  • 401(k) plan

  • Twice-yearly in-person offsites across the U.S.

  • Wellness benefits starting on your first day

Our Values

  • Fearless — Inspire and break down seemingly impossible walls

  • Fast — Launch fast with excellence; iterate to perfection

  • Lovable — Deliver happiness and 11-star experiences

  • Owners — Execute and run the business with ownership

  • Win-win — Create mutual value and earn trust for life

  • Inclusive — Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams

jobs.jobDescription:
Open call for Founders / Founding Teams (Product Management / Engineering roles)

In 1973 at Xerox PARC, Bob Metcalfe sketched a way for many computers to share a single wire — borrowing the throughput math from his study of Hawaii's ALOHAnet — and he and David Boggs built it and measured it until it held. Behind Ethernet was a two-person team that turned a contested idea into the measured standard now carrying almost all the world's wired traffic.

At Mercury, we’re looking to accelerate several of our AI products that our customers love like Command, CLI, and MCP. We’re building for ambitious people of all kinds, and are a company made of founders and small technical teams trying to change the world - as part of that, we’re taking open applications for founders or small technical teams (Eng+) that want to work together on building the AI products of the future. This isn't a fixed role. We expect the nature of work is changing, and small teams of people paired with AI product surface and autonomy to build can create 10x outcomes. Apply as a small team or as an individual

Here are some things you’ll do on the job:

  • Find the problem. Work close enough to customers that you spot what matters before anyone assigns it to you — then decide it's worth building.
  • Build and automate the workflow end to end using Command, CLI, MCP, and the rest of our AI stack.
  • Ship to customers fast — quick understanding, tight iteration, deploy.
  • Measure the impact honestly, then do the next one. Kill what didn't move; double down on what did.
  • Run as an autonomous team — pick the target, ship the thing, own the outcome.

You should:

  • Have shipped something real - a product, a tool, a company, or an open-source project people actually use.
  • Be dangerous across the stack: PMs who can prototype, engineers with product taste.
  • Have strong opinions about AI products and the judgment to recognize fast when one of them is wrong.
  • Hands experience building AI products with AI, and knowledge about RAG, evals, agent harnesses a plus
  • Move fast and measure. Expect most experiments to fail and treat that as the price of finding the ones that don't.
  • Care about craft where it's impactful and resist polishing what isn't.
  • Communicate clearly and own outcomes - we want real business impact, customer time/pain saved, and a path to scaling what works

Learn more about what we're building:

  • Mercury Command — Complete financial work end-to-end with AI. Tell Mercury what to do in natural language; it stages the action and executes with your approval.
  • Mercury MCP & CLI — Give your AI agents direct access to verified financial data, or work with your Mercury account straight from the terminal.
  • The bank of the future knows your business — Immad on what we're building toward and why now is the moment.

What happens next?

Submit your application and our recruiting team will follow up. We're genuinely open to connecting with founders and teams at any stage — whether you're a strong fit for something we're actively building toward right now, or this is the start of a longer relationship we pick back up when the opportunity is right. If you're building, we want to know you.

About the Role

The Director, Audit Transformation will lead the shift from traditional audit execution to an agentic operating model. Reporting to the Head of Audit, you will set the direction for how financial audit agents are designed, adopted, and scaled across our customer base.

You will serve as the connection point between the Fieldguide agentic platform and the profession it serves. In partnership with product, engineering, sales, and customer success, you will define the scope of the audit expertise behind an agentic operating model rather than layering agents onto legacy processes, including the documentation required to satisfy professional standards and withstand regulatory inspection. With Customer Success, you will establish the change management framework that guides firms from initial adoption through full transformation, built for consistent delivery at scale.

You will also support the Head of Audit on the strategic planning and special initiatives that translate audit strategy into execution and go to market initiatives.

This role calls for a leader with audit credibility earned through leading engagements, shaping methodology, or driving innovation within a leading firm, together with the conviction that professional judgment remains central to the audit. This is an opportunity to define how audit is delivered in the next decade, not to refine how it is delivered today.

What You’ll Do

Product Partnership

  • Serve as the audit domain expert in product discovery, prioritization, and roadmap planning for agent-based workflows, translating practitioner and firm needs into product specs

  • Work with AI architects and engineers to translate professional standards and practitioner judgment into the prompts, workflows, and guardrails behind our integrated methodologies and testing agents

  • Determine which procedures are suitable for agent execution, what level of autonomy is appropriate, and how output must be documented to satisfy professional standards and withstand regulatory inspection

  • Pressure-test new agent capabilities with practitioners before they ship, creating a tight feedback loop between the field, Methodology, and Product

Customer Transformation

  • Own, with Customer Success, the transformation motion that guides firms from initial adoption to full agentic audit transformation, including the playbook, maturity model, and program structure behind it

  • Equip Customer Success with the frameworks, content, and training to deliver transformation engagements repeatably and at scale, rather than one-off and bespoke

  • Serve as executive sponsor and audit subject-matter expert on transformation engagements with Fieldguide's most strategic accounts

  • Act as an escalation point on complex methodology and adoption issues

  • Monitor customer health and methodology fit, feeding what you learn back into the product and methodology roadmaps

  • Represent Fieldguide externally through written content, webinars, and speaking engagements such as AICPA ENGAGE and state CPA societies, and through relationships with standard-setters, regulators, and industry analysts

  • Monitor regulatory and standard-setting developments across the PCAOB, AICPA, and SEC, and translate the implications into Fieldguide's product, methodology, and messaging

Go-to-Market Support

  • Partner with Sales and Solutions Engineering on go to market opportunities, leading executive briefings, product demonstrations, and technical validation conversations with firm leadership

  • Represent Fieldguide on customer onsites, building credibility with both firm leadership and technical evaluators

jobs.jobDescription:
About the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank.

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit.

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:

  • Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.
  • Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.
  • Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.
  • Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.
  • Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.
  • Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.
  • Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.
  • Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.
  • Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.
  • Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.
  • Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.
  • Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.
  • Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.
  • Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.

What we’re looking for:

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development, quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.
  • Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.
  • Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.
  • Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.
  • Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.
  • High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.
  • Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.
  • Knowledge of Haskell

What success looks like:

  • Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.
  • Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.
  • Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.
  • Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.
  • Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.

*Mercury is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group, Column N.A., and Evolve Bank & Trust, Members FDIC.

About Us

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of advisory, audit, and tax practitioners at the world's largest CPA firms. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We're based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Goldman Sachs, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, and Y Combinator.

We value diversity, in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide's team is inclusive, driven, humble, and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture we are building, seeking teammates who are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

As a growth stage startup employee, you'll have the opportunity to build the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners' lives easier by eliminating up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide.

About the Role

Internal audit is being asked to do more with less. According to the IIA's 2026 North American Pulse of Internal Audit, the share of functions reporting budget cuts rose from 11% to 19% in a single year, while the share reporting increases fell from 34% to 23%, and staff cuts climbed from 11% to 18%. The audit universe keeps growing. The team does not.

As Staff Product Manager for Internal Audit, you will own the strategy for how Fieldguide wins this market and the roadmap that gets us there.

What You'll Do

  • Shape product strategy for Fieldguide's corporate internal audit line, from market entry through to a sequenced roadmap

  • Build enterprise-grade AI agents that increase efficiency, quality, and practitioner experience across each stage of the audit lifecycle from planning and risk assessment to audit execution and reporting.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams including customer success, sales, and marketing to gather feedback, communicate product strategy, and drive the introduction and adoption of product features

  • Work directly with Chief Audit Executives, VPs of Internal Audit, and Heads of IT Audit, including onsite, and bring what you learn back into the roadmap

Who You Are

  • 10+ years of product management experience

  • Experience with internal audit, SOX, risk, or another regulated compliance workflow, either as a practitioner or as a PM who has built software for that market.

  • Fluent in the vocabulary of the work: audit universe, entity-level controls, risk and control matrices, walkthroughs, deficiency severity, remediation, external auditor reliance.

  • Strong technical fluency: comfortable talking with engineers about LLM and agent architecture, evals, and tradeoffs without needing to write code.

  • Able to hold a strategic position under sustained pressure from commercial stakeholders, and to change it when the argument is genuinely good.

  • Comfortable working with detail-oriented, skeptical audiences and translating their workflow into product requirements.

More About Fieldguide

  • Win-win: Create mutual value and earn trust for life.

  • Inclusive: Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership

  • Flexible PTO

  • 401k

  • Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions

  • Technology and Work from Home reimbursement

Good marketing depends on systems that work: conversion signals that arrive accurately, audiences that stay current, and tools that make new ideas easier to try.

We’re hiring a Marketing Engineer to build and maintain those systems at Mercury. You’ll work directly with marketers to understand what they need, turn those needs into working integrations and tools, and keep what you build reliable after launch.

You’ll report to our Head of Growth Marketing as a hands-on individual contributor, partnering closely with Performance Marketing, Lifecycle, SEO, Data, and Engineering.

You’ll own the connections between our marketing platforms, including implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance. Data owns the shared customer-data foundation, warehouse pipelines and transformations, attribution methodology, and analytical models. Growth Engineering builds and maintains our GTM orchestration layer. You’ll work with both teams to make those systems useful in marketing.

Here are some of the things you’ll do:

  • Build and operate marketing integrations. Connect customer engagement, advertising, analytics, and other marketing platforms using APIs, webhooks, integration tools, and custom code. Test and deploy changes using Mercury’s shared development tools and review practices, and own monitoring and recovery when something breaks.
  • Own marketing tracking and conversion delivery. Maintain campaign tagging, cross-domain measurement, and browser- and server-side tracking. Investigate missing events, duplicate conversions, and discrepancies between platforms. Partner with Web and Product Engineering when fixes require changes to shared website or application code.
  • Make customer data usable in marketing. Connect approved attributes, audiences, and conversion signals to marketing platforms using tools such as Segment and Polytomic. Use SQL to validate results and trace problems across systems. Work with Data on source-data requirements and the return of marketing activity to shared datasets.
  • Maintain measurement and experimentation tools. Own GA4 configuration, including events, custom dimensions, platform connections, and reporting setup. Implement measurement definitions agreed with Data across tools such as GA4 and Rockerbox. Support website forms, experimentation tools, and the technical setup for SEO and AI-search experiments.
  • Set priorities and improve reliability. Own the roadmap for marketing integrations, tracking, and platform improvements with Growth Marketing leaders. Address recurring failures, manage platform configuration and access, document how systems work, and build reusable tools that help marketers launch and learn faster.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • A track record of independently building and maintaining software or integrations for marketing teams. You can write, test, debug, deploy, and maintain code — and explain the choices you made.
  • Hands-on experience with GA4, website event tracking, and advertising conversion integrations, including browser- and server-side implementations. You understand how identity, consent, and data quality affect measurement.
  • Practical SQL skills. You can inspect source data, validate an audience or conversion feed, and trace a discrepancy from the original event to its destination.
  • Experience connecting customer engagement, advertising, or marketing automation platforms through APIs and webhooks. You know how to handle authentication, failed requests, duplicate events, and changing platform requirements.
  • Clear communication and sound judgment. You can turn a marketer’s goal into technical requirements, prioritize competing requests, and work with Data and Engineering to resolve dependencies and ownership questions.

Our current stack includes Snowflake, Segment, Polytomic, Customer.io, Salesforce, Dato, GA4, Rockerbox, and major search and social advertising platforms. Experience with comparable systems is valuable; we don’t expect you to have used every tool.

jobs.jobDescription:
Who we are:

Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.

We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.

Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.

About the team:

Formic's Marketing Team is the growth engine behind our commercial expansion. We move fast, experiment boldly, and build systems that scale. We work in close lockstep with Sales, RevOps, and Leadership to generate pipeline, sharpen our message, and get in front of the right manufacturers at the right time. This team is small, high-impact, and driven - and we're looking for someone who can match that energy.

About this role:

As our Head of Marketing, you will build, optimize, and lead a scalable engine for creating demand and qualified pipeline. You will own how Formic shows up in the market, how we identify and reach the manufacturers we can help, and how we turn that engagement into high quality opportunities for Sales.

This is a broad, hands-on role spanning Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering and managing a team to deliver across those areas. You'll bring those capabilities together around a common goal: creating qualified pipeline and quantifying through data and insights what's driving it. As Formic grows, you'll help determine how the team and these capabilities evolve.

We're looking for someone who combines creativity with operating rigor. You'll set strategy, but you'll stay close enough to the work to understand what's actually happening. You'll establish clear priorities, ownership, and metrics, and make decisions based on results. When something works, you'll scale it. When it doesn't, you'll change it or stop doing it.

You'll also build and develop the team around you. That means setting clear expectations, delegating real ownership, coaching people to get better, and holding the team accountable for results. We want a leader who welcomes challenges, seeks out evidence that their assumptions may be wrong, and changes course when the data or the team tells them something different.

This is a builder role. One day you might be sharpening Formic's positioning; the next, reviewing pipeline performance with Sales, coaching an SDR, digging into why a campaign isn't converting, or working with a GTM Engineer to test a completely different way of reaching manufacturers. You should be equally comfortable asking "What should we try?" and "Did it work?"

We’re not looking for a standard B2B marketing playbook or activity for activity’s sake. We’re looking for a Head of Marketing who creates focus from ambiguity, turns experiments into learning, and builds repeatable systems that drive measurable business results.

You’ll bring a healthy appetite for the unconventional—challenging how things have always been done, proposing bold ideas, and testing them intelligently. We want the kind of imagination that makes people stop, pay attention, and think differently about industrial automation.

The next great idea in industrial marketing probably sounds a little crazy. Good. We want to hear it. Help us make industrial robotics impossible to ignore.

You will own the engine that feeds our sales and deployments.

In this role you will:

Own Brand & Marketing

  • Own Formic's marketing strategy and how we show up in the market.
  • Develop and continually sharpen our positioning, messaging, and story.
  • Translate Formic's technology, business model, and customer value proposition into messaging that resonates with manufacturers and their economic buyers.
  • Own content, creative, video, website, customer stories, events, campaigns, thought leadership, PR, product marketing, and other channels that build awareness and demand.
  • Develop differentiated messaging across industries, use cases, personas, and stages of the buying journey.
  • Demonstrated ability to conceive and execute original, unconventional marketing campaigns that break through industry norms, capture attention, and produce measurable business impact.
  • Turn customer outcomes, deployments, product capabilities, and what we're learning in the field into compelling content.
  • Build Formic's brand within manufacturing while ensuring our marketing investments support clear commercial objectives.

Own Demand & Pipeline Generation

  • Own the creation of qualified pipelines across Marketing, lead generation, SDR/outbound, ABM, events, paid, organic, partnerships, and emerging channels.
  • Establish clear pipeline goals and build repeatable systems to identify, engage, and qualify manufacturers that fit Formic's ideal customer profile, optimizing channel mix, conversion, and resources.
  • Lead and develop our Sales Development function, including targeting, prospecting strategy, messaging, sequencing, coaching, productivity, and performance.
  • Establish clear funnel definitions, ownership, lead routing, and follow-up processes to ensure every source of inbound and outbound interest is captured, acted upon, and effectively handed off to Sales.
  • Partner closely with Sales and RevOps on territory priorities, pipeline needs, lead quality, conversion, and feedback from the market.
  • Measure pipeline contribution, progression, conversion, and cost by source and channel, connecting marketing investments to closed-won revenue and informing where to invest, optimize, or stop.

Build Our GTM Innovation Capability

  • Lead our GTM Engineering capability, using AI, automation, data, enrichment, personalization, and emerging technologies to improve how we identify, reach, engage, and qualify potential customers.
  • Own the effectiveness and evolution of our marketing technology ecosystem, including CRM integrations, outbound platforms, lead routing, data quality, attribution, and reporting, in partnership with Sales and RevOps.
  • Build and optimize scalable systems for account identification, segmentation, prospecting, personalization, campaign execution, and lead management.
  • Evaluate existing tools and workflows, identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, integrate, consolidate, or eliminate work rather than defaulting to additional tools or headcount.
  • Drive disciplined experimentation across channels, technologies, data sources, and approaches, establishing clear hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and decisions about what to scale, change, or stop.
  • Ensure our GTM infrastructure is reliable, documented, and maintainable, with clear ownership, appropriate data governance, and minimal dependency on any single person or external partner.

Own the Funnel and the Numbers

  • Establish clear visibility into the entire funnel, from target account through qualified opportunity, pipeline progression, and revenue.
  • Define and own a focused set of metrics that measure pipeline creation, conversion, velocity, cost, channel effectiveness, and commercial impact.
  • Partner with Sales and RevOps to ensure reliable data, consistent reporting, and a shared understanding of performance.
  • Establish a disciplined operating cadence that translates performance insights into decisions about strategy, priorities, budget, and resources, holding the organization accountable for outcomes rather than activity.

Create Focus and Accountability

  • Translate broad company objectives into clear priorities, ownership, expectations, and measurable outcomes that connect the team's work to business goals.
  • Make disciplined decisions about priorities and resources, challenging assumptions, stopping initiatives that aren't delivering results, and adapting as we learn.
  • Stay close enough to the work to identify problems early, remove obstacles, and hold people accountable without becoming a bottleneck to execution.
  • Foster a culture of transparency, constructive challenge, and open communication about performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and lessons learned.
  • Establish accountability for external agencies, contractors, and technology partners, including deliverables, performance, costs, documentation, and continuity, while building sustainable processes that preserve institutional knowledge and support organizational change.

Build and Lead the Team

  • Lead and align af multidisciplinary organization spanning Marketing, content and creative, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering around shared commercial goals.
  • Build a high-performing team by establishing clear expectations, delegating meaningful ownership, coaching and developing talent, and addressing performance gaps directly.
  • Assess existing capabilities, recognize and develop the strengths of the people already here, and determine what additional skills and resources we'll need as we grow.
  • Hire thoughtfully and build organizational capabilities that create leverage, rather than adding unnecessary layers or headcount.
  • Foster a culture of creativity, curiosity, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement, where people feel empowered to challenge assumptions and solve problems.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • Experience building and leading Marketing, Growth, Demand Generation, or similarly broad functions in high-growth B2B companies, with measurable commercial results.
  • A track record of building, improving, and scaling marketing and pipeline-generation systems, not simply inheriting and managing established operations.
  • Deep understanding of B2B demand generation, funnel economics, segmentation, conversion, attribution, and how Marketing, SDR, and Sales work together to create and convert pipeline.
  • Experience developing differentiated positioning and messaging for complex products, markets, and buying decisions.
  • Strong technical fluency and demonstrated experience evaluating, integrating, and optimizing marketing technology, data, automation, and AI-enabled GTM systems, with the ability to diagnose problems and make informed architectural decisions.
  • An AI-native mindset, with demonstrated ability to apply emerging technologies, experiment rigorously, evaluate results, and turn successful approaches into scalable capabilities.
  • Strong people leadership, including building and developing teams, delegating meaningful ownership, addressing performance gaps, and leading effectively through growth and organizational change.
  • An operating style that combines creativity, analytical rigor, intellectual flexibility, and accountability, with the judgment to challenge assumptions, make difficult tradeoffs, and change course when evidence warrants it.
  • The ability to operate strategically and tactically, creating clarity from ambiguity, communicating effectively across functions, and staying close enough to execution to understand and solve problems.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience in manufacturing, industrial automation, robotics, industrial technology, or similarly complex B2B markets with long sales cycles and multiple decision-makers.
  • Experience directly building or leading SDR organizations, including account-based and territory-based outbound strategies.
  • Experience building or leading GTM Engineering, Growth Engineering, or similar technical growth capabilities.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, Formic has a marketing and pipeline-generation engine that we understand, measure, and know how to scale.

We know who we should target, how to reach them, which messages resonate, which channels create qualified opportunities, what those opportunities cost, and where we should invest next.

There is clear ownership across the funnel. Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering operate as one connected organization, with a tight feedback loop into Sales. The team knows what matters and what it's accountable for.

Experiments have hypotheses and measurable outcomes. Successful ideas become repeatable systems. Unsuccessful ones produce learning and stop consuming resources. Decisions about priorities, budget, and headcount are grounded in results.

Our marketing and GTM infrastructure is reliable, integrated, and well understood. We have confidence in our data, clear accountability for lead management, and systems that the team can operate and improve independently. Technology and vendor decisions are deliberate, economically justified, and aligned with our commercial priorities.

Most importantly, Sales has a consistent and growing flow of qualified opportunities, and we can explain what is creating them.

That's the engine you'll own.

Our Total Rewards:

At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:

  • Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
  • Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
  • Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
  • Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
  • Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
  • Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
  • Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
  • Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy

Compensation Philosophy

Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.

Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.

Compensation Range:

$145,000—$220,000 USD

What we look for:

We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!

  • Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
  • Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
  • Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
  • Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
  • Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
  • One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

Equal Opportunity Employment:

Formic is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to careers@formic.co.

jobs.jobDescription:
About the role:

As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical. Compliance is not only a requirement, but a competitive advantage that enables Mercury to move faster, build trust, and launch innovative products responsibly.

Nowhere is that more true than in AI. We believe we have a path to lead the US banking* industry into the AI era, and that how we choose to build and deploy AI will define our success over the next three years.

We are building first-party agentic products, headless and agent-accessible banking through our API and MCP, and the internal platforms that let us build with AI at speed. Core to all of it is great governance—these systems must run on one trusted system of access, logging, and data controls that meets the requirements of our banking ambitions.

We are seeking a Lead Compliance Risk Manager to serve as the compliance advisor for Mercury's AI products. This is a new, high-visibility role and the first dedicated compliance advisory seat covering AI at Mercury. You will be the leading authority on AI product compliance risk for the Compliance Team—shaping how we build, how we govern, and how we explain ourselves to our partners and regulators.

You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Legal, and Operations to ensure Mercury's AI products are compliant-by-design from concept through launch and scale. You will also help define the AI governance framework itself: the standards, controls, escalation paths, and documentation that allow a bank-partnered fintech to deploy agentic capabilities responsibly and at pace.

How this role fits alongside our other AI roles: this is a product compliance advisory role. Our Data & AI Governance team owns enterprise governance frameworks, responsible-AI standards, AI use case intake and inventory, and risk classification; Model Risk Management owns model inventory, tiering, and validation. You will be a close partner to and a major consumer of both—running our AI products through their processes, applying their standards to real product decisions, and bringing them the product-level detail they need to see. You will also help extend our existing product compliance playbooks to cover AI features, in partnership with your manager and the rest of the Product Compliance team. Your mandate is the products, not the program.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the subject matter expert and primary compliance advisor for Mercury's AI and agentic products, including Command, our API, and agentic access methods such as MCP and CLI.
  • Work closely with cross-functional risk and product teams to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a way that meets all relevant financial partner, regulatory compliance obligations, and our AI governance standards.
  • Ensure all processes and products under your area of responsibility comply with applicable rules and regulations. Stay up to date with changes to applicable regulations, supervisory guidance, and emerging AI-specific law, and implement necessary updates to impacted products to maintain compliance.
  • Support expansion for new product launches by scoping, defining, and communicating product and compliance requirements.
  • Work cross-functionally to drive remediation efforts for products within your defined scope.
  • Support the compliance function in defining and achieving departmental initiatives, maintaining relevant policies and procedures, developing documentation solutions, and liaising with auditors.
  • Mentor and provide strategic guidance to compliance colleagues as AI capabilities spread across every product domain, and contribute to building a strong culture of compliance across Mercury.
  • Work closely with our Risk team, which owns AI governance, as Compliance’s AI product expert to contribute product-level guidance to ongoing AI governance updates.

Core responsibilities:

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Operations, and Legal to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a manner that meets all relevant regulatory, financial partner, and network obligations.
  • Advise product and engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle—discovery, design, evaluation, launch, and iteration—to ensure AI products are compliant-by-design rather than reviewed after the fact.
  • Identify, assess, and document compliance risks specific to AI and agentic systems—including inaccurate or fabricated output, unauthorized or over-scoped agent action, inadequate consent and disclosure, unexplainable decisioning, disparate impact, data leakage across customers or organizations, prompt injection and third-party agent risk, and insufficient audit trail—and work cross-functionally to design pragmatic mitigation strategies.
  • Define the compliance requirements for the platforms AI is built on, in partnership with the teams that own them: the LLM gateway all internal traffic routes through, the internal app platform, agent orchestration frameworks, and the data access and governance layer.
  • Establish and refine AI-specific compliance standards for the department—what evidence a launch requires, what must be logged, what requires human review, what must be escalated, and what is out of bounds—and ensure those standards evolve as the organization and the technology grow.
  • Support new product launches and expansions by scoping, defining, and communicating compliance requirements clearly and early, including for co-marketing and distribution partnerships with third-party AI platforms.
  • Monitor regulatory, supervisory, and industry developments relevant to AI in financial services, assess impact, and drive implementation of required changes.
  • Own and oversee multiple concurrent high-impact AI compliance workstreams, holding project owners accountable for results and ensuring each aligns with department and company objectives.
  • Support remediation efforts for products within scope, including root cause analysis, corrective action planning, and execution tracking.
  • Partner with executive leadership, partner bank compliance teams, and external advisors to guide high-level decisions on AI direction, presenting data-driven recommendations.
  • Contribute to the broader Compliance function by supporting policy development, documentation standards, audit preparation, and examiner interactions.
  • Help build and reinforce a strong culture of compliance across Mercury through collaboration, education, and influence—including raising the AI fluency of the Compliance team itself, and developing scalable tools, templates, and frameworks others can reuse.

You should have:

  • 8+ years of experience in a compliance advisory, product compliance, or regulatory risk role, ideally within fintech or financial services, with a track record of being the recognized authority in your domain.
  • Demonstrated experience advising on AI, machine learning, or model-driven products in a regulated environment—or comparable experience standing up a new compliance domain where no playbook existed.
  • Working knowledge of the regulatory and supervisory framework relevant to AI in banking, including UDAAP, fair lending and ECOA/Reg B, FCRA and adverse action, Reg E and payments authorization, BSA/AML, GLBA and privacy, marketing and disclosure requirements, recordkeeping, complaint management, model risk management expectations, and third-party and vendor risk management guidance.
  • Familiarity with emerging AI-specific regimes and frameworks and the ability to form a practical view on their application—such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, state AI and automated decisioning laws.
  • Technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers on model behavior, evaluation and testing, agent permissioning and tool scoping, logging and observability, and data access controls—and to know which questions actually surface risk.
  • Deep experience partnering with product and engineering teams on regulatory and compliance matters across the product lifecycle, including on fast-moving launches with external dependencies.
  • Proven ability to own highly ambiguous, large-scale compliance problems and to create and execute a strategy to address them, without waiting for precedent.
  • Experience designing compliance frameworks that span multiple product lines or departments, and improving systems and processes so that compliance posture evolves alongside business growth.
  • Demonstrated success operating with senior stakeholders, including executives, partner banks, auditors, or regulators, and presenting data-driven recommendations that drive decisions.
  • Strong project management skills, including the ability to define problems, create execution plans, manage several high-impact initiatives at once, and drive outcomes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate regulatory and financial partner risk into terms stakeholder teams understand, and to resolve conflict around risk tolerance, resourcing, and timelines.
  • Experience mentoring mid-level compliance professionals and raising the capability of a team, not just delivering your own work.
  • Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with sound judgment on when to move and when to escalate.
  • Curiosity, adaptability, and genuine interest in engaging with frontier technology and the regulatory challenges that come with it.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

About Us

Fieldguide is the agentic AI-native platform for audit and advisory. We're establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by putting AI agents to work alongside the practitioners who verify how the economy actually operates.

The profession is facing a structural capacity problem. CPA exam candidates are at a 17-year low, and as many as 75% of today's CPAs are expected to retire over the next decade, while regulatory complexity and client expectations keep rising. We're building the system that closes that gap.

We've raised over $125M from Growth Equity by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Thomson Reuters, Floodgate, and Y Combinator. More than half of the top-100 U.S. CPA firms are customers, including several Big 4 firms, and we have the NPS to match. Our agents help practitioners save up to 75% of time on manual tasks and unlock over 4x capacity.

We're deliberate about how we operate. Our FFLOWI values (Fearless, Fast, Lovable, Owners, Win-Win, Inclusive) mean we launch fast and iterate to perfection, we solve problems without red tape, and we hold ourselves to 11-star experiences for customers who cannot afford to be let down.

About the Role

As Senior Manager, Product Strategy & Operations, you'll be the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market, turning strategy into execution across the product lifecycle. You'll build the operating systems that help our product teams make better decisions, ship with confidence, and prove measurable impact for the firms betting their delivery model on us.

This is the first dedicated hire in this function. You'll work as an extension of product leadership, balancing hands-on execution with strategic initiatives, and you'll build from zero rather than inherit. If ambiguity slows you down, this isn't the role.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and maintain Voice of Customer systems that synthesize signal from engagement partners, managers, and staff auditors, along with Solutions, Implementation, and Sales, into product signals teams can act on

  • Establish rigorous mechanisms for measuring product success and user impact i.e. dashboards, KPIs

  • Own the analysis behind major product bets: competitive positioning, where agent capabilities should expand next, and the unit economics of running agents at scale i.e. inference cost per engagement, cost-to-serve by segment, and what those trends imply for roadmap sequencing

  • Own and improve core product development processes, tooling, and team rituals: planning cycles, roadmap reviews, monthly business reviews

  • Build run-of-business systems that scale as we grow i.e. launch calendars, intake frameworks, RACI structures

  • Drive cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success

Who You Are

  • 6-8+ years in Product Operations, Product Management, product or corporate strategy, consulting, or a closely related operational role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company

  • You've built processes and programs from scratch and scaled them thoughtfully, not just inherited and maintained them

  • Strong ability to translate complex qualitative and quantitative data — usage metrics, feedback themes, retention signals — into clear recommendations and roadmap inputs. You can pull the data yourself rather than waiting on a queue

  • Proven ability to drive alignment across Product, GTM, and Engineering without direct authority

More about Fieldguide

Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:

  • Fearless - Inspire & break down seemingly impossible walls.

  • Fast - Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.

  • Lovable - Deliver happiness & 11 star experiences.

  • Owners - Execute & run the business with ownership.

  • Win-win - Create mutual value & earn trust for life.

  • Inclusive - Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams.

Some of our benefits include

  • Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership

  • Flexible PTO

  • 401k

  • Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions

  • Technology & Work from Home reimbursement

  • Flexible work schedules

Mercury is one of the fastest-growing companies in fintech, and we’re building something unusual in the category: a premium brand that people genuinely want to engage with.

We’re looking for a Head of Social & Community to shape how Mercury shows up in the world and deepen our relationship with the founders, entrepreneurs, and businesses we serve. You’ll lead our work across social, community, creators and influencers, and merch — bringing these channels together to build a brand people want to participate in, not just hear from.

This is a role for someone who wants to push beyond the standard brand playbook. You’ll have the opportunity to develop campaigns, partnerships, experiences, and ideas that most financial brands wouldn’t attempt, while growing and fostering one of the most engaged customer communities in fintech. You’ll report to our Head of Brand, lead a small but mighty team, and have the opportunity to expand as the function scales.

*Mercury is a financial technology company, not a FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group, Column N.A., Members FDIC.

In this role, you’ll:

  • Set the strategy for social and community at Mercury, connecting social, creators and influencers, and merch into a cohesive ecosystem that grows our audience, deepens engagement, and builds long-term brand affinity.
  • Shape and amplify Mercury’s voice across channels, setting a high bar for the ideas, writing, creative, and experiences we put into the world.
  • Develop breakthrough campaigns and programs that give people a reason to talk about, participate in, and advocate for Mercury - from an unexpected social idea to a creator partnership or piece of merch.
  • Connect our community work to the broader marketing organization, partnering closely with Brand, Creative, Growth, Product Marketing, Support, and others to turn company priorities into bigger ideas and bring insights from our community back into Mercury.
  • Own the goals, budgets, measurement, and operating rhythms for the function, balancing creative ambition with analytical rigor to understand what’s working and where to invest next.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary team of three, creating clarity across distinct areas of work and growing the organization as our ambitions expand.

What you’ll bring:

  • Experience leading a team and meaningful budget across social, merch, creator or influencer partnerships, or related brand and community disciplines.
  • Exceptional creative and editorial taste. You can write a great post, spot when a concept isn’t working, give incisive feedback on creative, and maintain a high bar without becoming a bottleneck.
  • A systems mindset. You know how to connect channels and individual moments to a larger story, building programs that compound into brand equity rather than a collection of one-offs.
  • Strong cross-functional instincts and the ability to be connective tissue across teams, bringing together different priorities while keeping the customer and community at the center.

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of assurance and audit practitioners specifically within cybersecurity, privacy, and financial audit. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We’re based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Elad Gil, and more.

We value diversity — in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide’s team is inclusive, driven, humble and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture that we are building, seeking teammates that are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

We make audit practitioners’ lives easier by bringing together up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide.

We are hiring a hands-on FP&A Manager to serve as the analytical engine of our planning, reporting, and decision support. You will own core planning cycles and the reporting that goes to our executive team and board, build the KPI infrastructure that tells us how the business is really performing, and support the strategic work that comes with scaling toward IPO. This role begins as an individual contributor with a clear path to building and leading a team as the function grows.

  • Prepare monthly and quarterly reporting packages with variance analysis and written commentary that explains the drivers, not just the deltas.

  • Build and maintain board and investor reporting materials in partnership with the Head of FP&A and the VP of Finance.

  • Improve our planning and reporting infrastructure, including the systems, data flows, and source-of-truth definitions that connect our ERP, CRM, and planning tools.

  • Partner with department leaders on headcount planning, spend management, and monthly budget reviews.

jobs.jobDescription:
In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem.

Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what deserves attention, what to do next. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard.

Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Key responsibilities:

  • Build a personal banking experience so good that people tell their friends and colleagues about it
  • Own the metrics, product strategy and the propositions we take to our customers, covering personal money management, banking, savings, investments, money movement, and in the future, lending
  • Set the craft bar: sweat the details — copy, latency, empty states — that decide whether a consumer product feels inevitable rather than adequate
  • Drive the use of AI in products where it makes the experience meaningfully better
  • Build and scale the org: recruit and lead a high-performing PM team, instill strong build discipline, develop future leaders, and set a cadence and culture that drives pace and quality
  • Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound, including how personal banking connects to the businesses Mercury already serves
  • Make reliability and trust product features: own uptime, correctness, latency, and support outcomes, and be measured on them
  • Align the ecosystem: bring product, engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive strategy

Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:

  • A consumer product leader with taste: you have built products millions of people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work
  • You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails
  • An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation-oriented approach
  • 10+ years building consumer products, including time owning a product's growth and economics, not only its roadmap
  • 5+ years leading product managers: hiring, coaching, org design, and performance management
  • Experience launching and scaling 0-1 products, alongside operating a large product with real customers on it
  • Exceptional cross-functional leadership across engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, and partners
  • Nice to have: banking, payments, or fintech experience. We can teach you the rails; we cannot teach product judgment
  • Sound judgment in a regulated environment: you balance a delightful experience with the controls a banking product requires, and know which corners are never worth cutting
